newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-METS USE FIVE LATE HOMERS TO BEAT PIRATES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-METS USE FIVE LATE HOMERS TO BEAT PIRATES.

text.p: The New York Mets went on a home run spree to erase a five-run deficit, erupting for nine runs over the last three innings with the help of five round-trippers for a 10-8 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates on Sunday.
John Olerud homered in the eighth and ninth innings and Butch Husky, Matt Franco and Todd Hundley also contributed to New York's late home run derby.
The Mets picked up three runs in the seventh on Huskey's solo shot and Franco's two-run blast and trailed 7-4 heading into the eighth.

Pittsburgh starter Francisco Cordova walked Edgardo Alfonzo to start the eighth and Chris Peters came in to face Olerud, who sent the first pitch over the centre-field fence. Hundley followed by hitting his team-leading 19th homer, tying the game at 7-7, and Luis Lopez added an RBI double to put the Mets in front.
In the ninth, Alfonzo singled and Olerud drove Rich Loiselle's 2-2 pitch over the right-field fence for his 13th homer and a 10-7 lead.
"Those were some good at bats," said Olerud. "I was swinging the bat good all day."
Added New York manager Bobby Valentine: "Cordova was pitching great but before you knew it we were back in it. John Olerud has given us the most consistent bat all year."
Ricardo Jordan (1-2) pitched the seventh and surrendered a homer to Kevin Young, but got the win.
At Colorado, Barry Bonds belted his 19th home run of the season and Shawn Estes won his seventh straight decision as the San Francisco Giants beat the Rockies 7-4.
Bonds staked the Giants to a 1-0 lead in the fourth with his 11th homer in 22 games off starter Roger Bailey.
Jeff Kent and Damon Berryhill also had solo homers for the Giants and Darryl Hamilton and Bill Mueller each contributed three hits and an RBI.
Estes (11-2) allowed two runs and eight hits in six innings and struck out seven. Bailey (8-6) was tagged for five runs and 10 hits in six innings.
In Atlanta, Fred McGriff's seventh-inning triple scored Chipper Jones with the go-ahead run as the Braves rallied past the Philadelphia Phillies 6-5 to complete a sweep of the four-game series.
Keith Lockhart had a pinch-hit grand slam in the sixth for Atlanta, which rallied from a 5-0 deficit after Phillies starter Scott Ruffcorn left the game with a no-hitter after 5 1/3 innings.
Ruffcorn was replaced when he lost control in the sixth, issuing a walk, a wild pitch and a hit batter. The Braves pushed five runs across in the inning.
In Chicago, Brad Ausmus and Derek Bell drove in three runs apiece to lead the Houston Astros to a 10-8 win over the Cubs.
Ausmus had a three-run double in the fifth and Bell had a homer in the first and a two-run single in the eighth.
Rey Sanchez and Jose Hernandez homered for the Cubs, who banged out 16 hits in a losing effort.

Houston starter Tommy Greene went 4 1/3 innings but was unable to get the win despite a 7-0 lead. Blas Minor came on the fifth and tossed a scoreless sixth to notch the win. Cubs starter Terry Mulholland (5-9) allowed seven runs and seven hits for the loss.
In Los Angeles, Pedro Astacio went eight innings to notch his first win since May 1 and Eric Karros homered and drove in four runs as the Dodgers pounded the San Diego Padres 10-3.
Astacio (4-7) allowed three runs and six hits over eight innings to snap a seven-game losing streak. He retired 12 straight batters between the third and seventh innings.
Karros knotted the game at 2-2 in the first with his 16th homer, a two-run shot off starter Danny Jackson (1-6).
With the Dodgers up 4-2 in the fifth, Karros lined the first pitch off the right-centre field fence, scoring Brett Butler and Wilton Guerrero.
At Florida, Bobby Bonilla hit a sacrifice fly to cap a four-run first inning and homered in the fourth to lead the Marlins to a 5-3 victory over the Montreal Expos.
Kurt Abbott had an RBI triple and Moises Alou tripled to centre with two aboard for a 3-0 Marlins lead. Alou scored on Bonilla's sac fly.
Bonilla's homer in the fourth off Carlos Perez (8-5) made it 4-0.
Al Leiter (7-5) allowed three runs and three hits over 6 2/3 innings for the win.

In Cincinnati, Ron Gant's one-out bloop single in the top of the 12th inning scored Danny Sheaffer with the winning run as the St Louis Cardinals outlasted the Reds 6-5 for their seventh win in nine games.
There were two rain delays totalling two hours, 53 minutes, including one with the game tied 5-5 in the 10th, before the Cards finally won.

Sheaffer led off the 12th with a single off Hector Carrasco (1-2), the fifth Reds pitcher. Delino DeShields sacrificed him to second and Gant blooped a hit in front of right fielder Willie Greene to bring home the winning run.
